card.title: MealSync
card.subtitle: AI-Assisted Household Meal Planning Platform
card.summary: AI-assisted household meal planning platform. Collaborative meal scheduling, recipe management, and automated grocery lists powered by Google Gemini. 77 automated tests, 93% AI service coverage. Built with FastAPI, React, and PostgreSQL.

detail.overview: MealSync is a collaborative web app for household meal planning and grocery shopping. It uses Google Gemini for recipe generation, with shared meal scheduling and automated grocery lists. A team project for CN7021 Advanced Software Engineering, built with FastAPI and React, with a layered backend and 93% AI service test coverage.

contentCards.markdown:
### Architecture

- **4-layer backend**: API (FastAPI + Pydantic), Service, Repository (7 domain repos), Model (8 entities with UUIDs)
- **SQLAlchemy + Alembic** for schema management and migrations
- **JWT + bcrypt** for authentication
- **Google Gemini AI** with structured prompting and response validation
- **Pytest**: 77 tests, 93% AI service coverage, all external calls mocked
- **GitHub Actions** CI/CD with Codecov integration

### Features

**Households**: invite-code based multi-user workspaces with role-based access (admin/member).

**Recipes & Pantry**: full recipe management with ingredient categorisation, search, and pantry tracking across 15 categories.

**Meal Planning**: calendar-based scheduling with recipe linking, serving adjustments, and per-member assignments. Bulk creation via atomic transactions for AI-generated plans.

**AI (Google Gemini)**: generates recipes and weekly meal plans from household preferences. Degrades gracefully when the service is unavailable.

**Grocery Lists**: auto-generated from planned meals with item categorisation and purchase tracking.

problem.title: Challenge: Reliable AI Service Testing
problem.issue: Gemini API calls are expensive, non-deterministic, and fail in CI/CD, making high coverage for AI features impractical without a proper isolation strategy.
problem.impact: Without mocking, tests would require live API keys, incur costs, and produce flaky results that break CI pipelines.

solution.title: Solution: Mock-Based Testing Strategy
solution.implementation: Used `unittest.mock.patch` to intercept all Gemini calls and replaced them with realistic JSON fixtures. Dependency injection kept AI services isolated from business logic. Tests tagged with `@pytest.mark.ai` for selective execution.
solution.result: 93% coverage on `ai_service.py` (60 tests covering network failures, invalid responses, and timeout handling), all running cost-free without API keys.

problem.title: Challenge: Unpredictable AI Response Formats
problem.issue: Gemini returns JSON inconsistently: sometimes in markdown code fences, sometimes as plain text with commentary. Direct `json.loads()` would crash on valid data in an unexpected wrapper.
problem.impact: Any format variation would cause a feature failure, showing users cryptic errors instead of their meal plans.

solution.title: Solution: Three-Tier JSON Extraction
solution.implementation: Implemented `_extract_json_from_response()` with a fallback chain: (1) direct `json.loads()`, (2) regex strip of markdown fences, (3) pattern match to find JSON within surrounding text. Each tier falls through on failure.
solution.result: Zero parsing failures in production across all response formats. Clear error messages surface only when the AI returns genuinely malformed data.

timeline.title: Iteration 1: Foundation & Authentication
timeline.description: Set up 4-layer FastAPI backend with SQLAlchemy + Alembic. Implemented JWT auth with bcrypt. Built household CRUD with invite codes. Scaffolded React + TypeScript frontend.

timeline.title: Iteration 2: Recipe & Ingredient Management
timeline.description: Recipe APIs with full data model (prep time, difficulty, cuisine). Ingredient database with 15 categories and 18 unit types. Many-to-many recipe-ingredient relationships. Pantry tracking with search.

timeline.title: Iteration 3: Meal Planning & Grocery Lists
timeline.description: Calendar-based meal scheduling with recipe linking and per-member assignments. Grocery list generation from planned meals with item categorisation and purchase tracking.

timeline.title: Iteration 4: AI Integration & Testing
timeline.description: Integrated Gemini API with structured prompting and response validation. 77 automated tests, 93% AI service coverage, all external calls mocked. GitHub Actions CI/CD with Codecov.

timeline.title: Iteration 5: Polish & Deployment
timeline.description: Responsive UI, loading states. IEEE SRS with 9 architecture diagrams. COCOMO effort estimation (~24 person-months). Deployed to Vercel. Submitted for CN7021.
